record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: If X ⊆ N^N is nonmeager and Y ⊆ N^N is dominating, does there exist a Borel set H ⊆ N^N × N^N such that every meager subset of N^N is contained in the vertical section Hx for some x in X ∪ Y?

evidence.quote: Assume that X ⊆ NN is nonmeager and Y ⊆ NN is dominating. Is there a Borel set H ⊆ NN × NN such that every meager set is contained in Hx for some x ∈ X ∪ Y?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ denote the Baire space, equipped with the product topology induced from the discrete topology on $\mathbb{N}$. A subset $M\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is meager if it is a countable union of nowhere dense sets, and nonmeager otherwise. A set $Y\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is dominating if for every $g\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ there exists $f\in Y$ such that $g(n)\le f(n)$ for all but finitely many $n$. For a set $H\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\times\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ and $x\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, let $H_x=\{y\in\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}:(x,y)\in H\}$ denote the vertical section of $H$ at $x$.

Suppose $X\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is nonmeager and $Y\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ is dominating. Does there exist a Borel set $H\subseteq \mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}\times\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ such that for every meager set $M\subseteq\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ there exists $x\in X\cup Y$ with $M\subseteq H_x$?
